issues.description: The problem description asks students to implement a method named printFarmSong() (see UML and Part 3 instructions), but both the template and the provided solution use a method named singFarmSong() instead. This name mismatch between the specification and the code can confuse students about which method to implement or test against and may lead to incorrect implementations or failing tests if the expected name differs.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across the specification, template, and solution. Either update the problem statement to instruct students to implement singFarmSong(), or rename the template/solution method to printFarmSong() (and update references) so the expected method name in the instructions matches the code.

issues.description: The problem statement repeatedly refers to a method named printFarmSong() (UML and task instructions), but both the template and the reference solution declare and use a method named singFarmSong(). This mismatch can confuse students: the instructions ask them to implement printFarmSong(), yet the starter files only provide singFarmSong(), and the solution also uses singFarmSong(). Students may implement the wrong method name or search for a non-existent method in the template.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method name across artifacts. Either update the problem statement to refer to singFarmSong() everywhere (so instructions match the template and solution), or rename the method in the template and solution from singFarmSong() to printFarmSong() and update usages accordingly so all artifacts use the same identifier.
